items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: although Glenn and I were good friends and we were later to play with the Ray Noble band

ctx.x: So I went over to hear this great player and Pee Wee was at the bar and we waited about a half hour and there appeared at the door, the speakeasy door, a man with a little cap, a button cap, a corduroy Norfolk suit, shoes -- trousers halfway up his legs -- I can't remember the shoes now -- but anyway, I think they were suede shoes and he had a trombone, not in a case, but in a little velvet bag. He took it out of the bag, put it together and played with no accompaniment, some of the finest music I ever have heard…

my life. I absolutely flipped over hearing him and I went back to Pollack that night, and I said, I heard the best jazz trombone player in the world. Well, But, of course, Glenn Miller wasn't I don't think too happy, I don't think, having heard me say that, but anyway, -- although Glenn and I were good friends and we were later to play with the Ray Noble band. Pollard heard Jack Teagarden play one chorus and hired him. Bud,
Incidentally, I remember riding in the front of the car with Jack doing the same thing on his mouthpiece in the back of the car.
